class: An account press whose result was assumed, not read; and an account's scope (one employer or a whole portal) never asked
symptom: Waystar (Workday), 1-2 October: 'created, not yet verified' logged six times after Create Account, each followed by a refused sign-in, with nothing kept of what the page said -- whether the account was ever made could not be told. Segra (Dayforce), 16 September: refused, on a portal whose one account serves every Dayforce employer. A refused password with no account on record always stopped for the owner.
site: Every ATS with candidate accounts; Dayforce, UKG and iCIMS's shared login for the scope
root_cause: fill_create_account_form decided the outcome from two checks (two password boxes still showing; a validation error) and otherwise assumed the account was made; the page after the press was never read as an account state, logged in the site's words or saved. Accounts were recorded and decided per employer only, so a portal with one shared login was treated like Workday: create first. The decision table had no way to ask the site whether an unknown account exists, so 'wrong email or password' with no record went to the owner.
why_tests_missed: Test pages after Create Account were either the account form again or a signed-in page; none showed a blank page, a banner on a different page, or nothing at all. The decision table was tested state by state for one employer's site; nothing tested it over every memory, or for a shared login.
fix: _account_click_result reads the page after every Create Account and Sign In press as an account state, logs ACCOUNT_RESULT with the site's own words, and saves a screenshot and the page text (secrets hidden) in logs/account_steps/. A create press after which the page shows no account step, no message and no application is reported as failed and not recorded; an 'already exists' banner on the next page goes to sign-in; a verify message opens the link at once. sites/accounts.py names the shared logins; there the table signs in first and the account is recorded once for the portal (record_key). A refused password for an account with no record, on a page offering Create Account, opens Create Account so the site says whether it exists; 'exists' after a refused sign-in goes to the owner's reset rule.
prevention: Every press that changes account state is followed by one reading of the page that names the result and keeps the evidence; nothing is recorded on a guess. Model whose account it is (one employer, or a portal's shared login) from the start, and test the decision table over every combination of its memory, not one case at a time.
